strategy_reasoning: This is a gas-liquid oxidative amidation requiring slug flow, so diameters below 0.75 mm are excluded to prevent channeling and ensure proper gas-liquid contact. Since the reaction is not photochemical, larger diameters (up to 2.0 mm) are permissible to manage pressure drop while maintaining enhanced laminar mixing. The sampling range spans from aggressive short-residence times (tau/3) to longer times (2x) to bracket the kinetic target and literature value, ensuring the 3x intensification mandate is tested against selectivity benefits.

problem_statement.flow_justification_note: Oxidative amidation typically requires molecular oxygen as a stoichiometric oxidant. Flow chemistry is highly justified to enhance gas-liquid mass transfer (O2 solubility) and control exotherms associated with oxidation, especially given the short residence time (3-4 min).
ambiguities: Confirm if O2 is supplied from air or pure O2 to determine pressure requirements.
Clarify if the reaction is catalytic (e.g., Cu, Fe) or stoichiometric in oxidant, as this affects catalyst retention strategies in flow.
Dioxane is a high-boiling solvent; confirm if product isolation requires solvent swap or if it can be removed directly.
